newsitem.title: BRAZIL: High Brazil oil imports continued in Oct - Malan.
newsitem.headline: High Brazil oil imports continued in Oct - Malan.

text.p: The high amount of crude oil and oil products imported into Brazil continued in October after September's surge was largely blamed for that month's larger-than-expected trade deficit, Brazilian Finance Minister Pedro Malan said.
Malan told Reuters late Monday that oil imports had, however, ceased now.
In September, oil purchases by state oil firm Petrobras totalling over $200 million were largely blamed for a $655 million monthly deficit.
"They continued a little in October but it won't happen again," Malan said.
Industry analysts attribute the increased imports to a stockbuilding by Petrobras as a hedge in anticipation of higher prices as well as increased consumption based on economic recovery.
Predictions for the trade deficit in October range as high as $1.0 billion, causing nervousness in the markets. October's trade balance was due to be announced either later this week or early next.
